subject.title: Approvals lost on gateway restart — stale callback buttons show confusing error

question: Should restart-stale exec/plugin approvals be deliberately invalidated with clear recovery UX, or should pending approvals be persisted and restored across gateway restarts?
rationale: The implementation choice changes the privileged approval trust boundary: fail-closed UX is simpler and safer, while persistence needs a durable state and replay model for approvals that authorize command execution.

options.title: Invalidate on restart
options.body: Treat gateway restart as approval expiry and make all user-facing approval paths tell the operator to re-request the action.

options.title: Persist with replay guards
options.body: Store pending approvals in SQLite with expiry, requester/approver binding, replay limits, and restart cleanup tests before restoring them after restart.

options.title: Split UX and persistence
options.body: Land the explicit stale/restart copy first and track durable approval persistence as a separate security design item.

recommendation.title: Invalidate on restart
recommendation.body: Treat gateway restart as approval expiry and make all user-facing approval paths tell the operator to re-request the action.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central gateway approval and callback paths are most recently tied to this author in current-main history.
